newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BRILLIANT KLOS SAVES BORUSSIA THREE POINTS AT ATLETICO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRILLIANT KLOS SAVES BORUSSIA THREE POINTS AT ATLETICO.

text.p: Goalkeeper Stefan Klos virtually guaranteed Borussia Dortmund a place in the quarter-finals of the European Cup with a superb performance in a 1-0 win at Atletico Madrid in the Champions' League on Wednesday.
"Atletico were very strong but we had Stefan Klos," said Borussia coach Ottmar Hitzfeld, whose side have won all three of their Group B games.
Hitzfeld's team also enjoyed a hefty dose of luck as Atletico squandered a hatful of chances to equalise Stefan Reuter's 50th-minute goal.
Atletico opened strongly and the game was only a few minutes old when Serbian midfielder Milinko Pantic forced the first fine save out of Klos.
But as the Germans tightened up at the back the Spaniards lost the fluency in midfield which had taken them to emphatic wins in their two previous Champions' League games.

Pantic, who was well marked by Scotsman Paul Lambert, and Czech international Radek Bejbl both seemed out of sorts for Atletico, while forward Kiko Narvaez was clearly short of match practice after returning from injury.
For Borussia, Brazilian sweeper Julio Cesar was in fine form despite playing with a muscle injury that brought about his substitution during the second half.
"In marking Juan Eduardo Esnaider Julio Cesar was fantastic," Atletico coach Radomir Antic said. "But I don't feel we're inferior to Borussia."
Borussia's best chance of the first half came after 27 minutes when a long-range free-kick from Julio Cesar was blocked and Lambert brushed the post with a fine shot from the rebound.
Just before halftime Klos made a superb close-range save from Esnaider after the Argentine had slipped his marker at a corner.

Esnaider went close again just after the break but moments later the tables were turned as Reuter drove down the right into the area and rode a challenge in which the ball appeared to hit his hand before leaving Atletic keeper Jose Molina with no chance.
The Germans had further chances but, after Julio Cesar was substituted, Esnaider found room up front and forced several more fine saves out of Klos.
Klos also stopped a well-struck Pantic free-kick 12 minutes from time as Atletico pressed desperately for an equaliser.

Atletico's Diego Simeone and Borussia's Joerg Heinrich and Juergen Kohler will miss the next Champions' League game -- which is between the same sides -- after picking up their second yellow cards in the competition.

Atletico Madrid: 1-Jose Molina, 3-Toni Munoz, 4-Roberto Solozabal, 6-Santi Denia, 15-Juan Carlos Aguilera (5-Juan Lopez 78), 20-Delfi Geli, 10-Milinko Pantic, 14-Diego Simeone, 24-Radek Bejbl (17-Juan Carlos Gomez 75), 9-Juan Eduardo Esnaider, 19-Kiko Narvaez

Borussia Dortmund: 1-Stefan Klos, 5-Julio Cesar (16-Martin Kree 67), 14-Paul Lambert, 15-Juergen Kohler, 7-Stefan Reuter, 8- Michael Zorc, 17-Joerg Heinrich, 18-Lars Ricken (Jovan Kirovski 71), 20-Wolfgang Feiersinger, 23-Rene Tretschok (11-Heiko Herrlich 86), 9-Stephane Chapuisat.
